messages:
alex-custsuccess: quick heads-up — enterprise customer reported a billing spike overnight + intermittent 401s and 503s. They also said performance degraded (p90 token latency went from 120ms -> 800ms). Can we triage?

maria-sre: saw a ticket, pulled metrics. There's a correlating latency bump around 02:10 UTC and a burst of auth failures. Investigating rate-limiter + auth service.

jon-security: tagging sec team. customer mentioned audit logs missing for a ~20m window during the spike; also forwarded a pen-test finding about KMS alias enumeration we retested last month. Could be related?

lee-eng: repro steps from customer attached. curl example they used: `curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'` returns 401 intermittently, and when it returns 200 it's slow.

sam-redteam: quick note from pen test: we observed a timing side-channel when alias lookup failed — but that was low-confidence. We flagged it as medium then. If auth failures line up with KMS calls failing, that could explain both 401s and audit gaps.

maria-sre: look at infra logs: around spike we had a flurry of KMS throttling errors from one region: `KMSThrottlingException` interleaved with `RequestTimeout`. I'll paste sample: ```[02:10:12 UTC] KMS ThrottleID=xyz KMSThrottlingException: Rate exceeded```

jon-security: that maps to customer region eu-west-1 per their support ticket. Are we sure those KMS errors are internal to our managed KMS integration and not the customer's key policy?

lee-eng: checked the key usage metrics — our vault pushed ~3x normal crypto ops because of an automated retry loop in the auth client after a transient 500. So retries + sync locking likely saturated the KMS connection pool. That would also suppress audit writes if the audit producer depends on the same token exchange path.

alex-custsuccess: customer says they saw audit events missing between 02:09:45 and 02:29:10. They need evidence for compliance.

jon-security: ok we need a remediation + evidence pack. Proposed steps: 1) capture KMS debug logs + throttle counters for eu-west-1 2) produce timeline mapping user requests -> token exchange -> KMS calls -> audit producer write attempts 3) retest pen finding vector against repro environment and confirm severity.

sam-redteam: I'm available to run the retest. I want to confirm the attacker model: in the original finding we could enumerate aliases with ~100ms variance when alias existed vs not. If the KMS was throttled the timing signal may amplify. That could raise severity.

maria-sre: I've started exporting audit producer logs from the timeframe and snapshotting the KMS request ids. Attaching sample logs to the ticket. Note: some entries show `audit_write_failed: downstream_timeout`.

lee-eng: can reproduce locally by forcing a 5xx on the token exchange endpoint then running a 10rps client for 3m. Reproduction script: ```for i in $(seq 1 300); do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $FAULTY" https://api... || echo "fail $i"; sleep 0.5; done``` Observed KMS error spike and audit queue backlog.

alex-custsuccess: customer asked if this is a billing bug or an attack. Any quick answer?

jon-security: initial assessment: not an active exploit of KMS keys but a combination of retries + throttling causing cascading failures. If redteam retest shows alias enumeration improves under throttling we may need to bump severity from medium -> high for the pen finding.

sam-redteam: I'll run the retest against a staging cluster with induced KMS throttling and share timing samples and PoC. ETA ~2 hours.

maria-sre: mitigation in flight: rate-limiter patch deployed to token-exchange (limits retry storm), and we enabled a short-circuit fallback that stops flood retries when KMS returns throttle. Rolling out to eu-west-1 now.

lee-eng: also added a backoff in the audit producer to persist to local buffer before failing hard — should reduce missing audit events during transient KMS issues.

jon-security: once sam posts retest results we'll decide severity and whether to require a postmortem for compliance. For now ask customer: we will provide a signed timeline + raw logs for 02:00-02:40 UTC and an explanation of remediation steps.

alex-custsuccess: done — letting customer know we can share logs and remediation plan and offering a call. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

sec-bot: Automated note: incident candidate created (INC-2026-1843). Assigned to maria-sre, jon-security.

sam-redteam: retest update: induced 429s on KMS and re-ran alias probe. Observed timing delta increase from ~100ms -> ~320ms in alias existence probe. Attaching CSV of samples. This makes the enumeration much more reliable under throttling.

jon-security: given the amplification under throttling, I'm recommending we elevate the pen finding severity to High and add a mitigation requirement: implement indistinguishable error paths + constant-time responses for alias lookups, and KMS request quota isolation.

lee-eng: agreed on isolation. For immediate mitigation we can add jittered constant-time responses for alias endpoints and tweak retry caps. We'll schedule a design review with infra.

maria-sre: eu-west-1 mitigations rolled, audit backfill job started for missing events. I'll keep the log bundle ready for customer export.

alex-custsuccess: customer is good with the interim plan, requested SLA credit estimate for the billing spike. Finance pinged.

jon-security: final action items: sam to upload PoC and CSV, lee to PR mitigation for alias timing, maria to upload logs + audit backfill evidence, alex to coordinate customer comms. We'll reconvene after PR review.

alex-custsuccess: thanks everyone — I'll update the ticket and close the loop with customer after we have the PoC and logs.
